subject: Post-demo recap: infer cost matrix, hyperscaler deltas, and next tests
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Srinivas <rajiv@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: infer cost matrix, hyperscaler deltas, and next tests

Hi Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

What we covered
- High-level differentiators: Redwood’s unified runtime (hosted / dedicated / private) gives predictable per-token economics via batching + prefix/KV cache and quantization.
- Hyperscaler comparison: hyperscaler endpoints simplify ops but often hide queuing/burst behavior and have higher per-token uplift at low volumes.
- Key commercial ask from you: apples-to-apples per-1M token comparisons, plus an atlas of latency vs. cost for your expected traffic shape.

Assumptions we’ll test (proposed)
- Workload: mixed chat + completion mix (~70% short chat, 30% long form), average seq = 250 tokens.
- Batching scenarios: small (concurrency 1–4), medium (8–32), and aggressive (64+).
- Cache hit rates to model: 10%, 30%, 60% (we’ll show how cache reduces host compute).

Proposed short experiments (2–3 days)
1) 1M token probe (hosted): measure token cost, p50/p95 latency, and effective cache hit rate.
2) Dedicated probe (reserved pool): same dataset, measure throughput and cold-starts.
3) Hyperscaler baseline: reproduce with your hyperscaler account (we’ll help set traffic pattern) and compare unit delta.

Ask from Nimbus
- Permission to run the 1M-token probe on a small sample namespace and point us at a sample of recent conversational logs (anonymized).
- Confirm preferred region (us-west1 was mentioned).
- Any constraints on synthetic traffic vs. production shadowing?

Attachments: redwood-1m-token-cost-model.xlsx (contains our initial cost assumptions and quick calc for hosted vs. dedicated vs. hyperscaler).

Next steps
- If you’re good with the plan: Ben will schedule the 2-hour bench session and produce the benchmark plan; we’ll share step-by-step runbooks and a Drive folder.
- If you need different cache hit brackets or a different avg sequence length, tell us and we’ll update.

Thanks — I’ll hold off scheduling until you confirm the dataset access and region.

Best,
Irene
Product Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-1m-token-cost-model.xlsx]

From: Rajiv Srinivas <rajiv@nimbushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health - Platform Team <ops@nimbushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: infer cost matrix, hyperscaler deltas, and next tests

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before you run anything:

1) Cache assumptions: when you say 60% hit rate at the high end, is that prefix caching (conversation reuse) or response-level dedup? Our logs show a lot of repeated system prompts across patients, but user prompts are fairly unique. We’d like a breakdown of both.

2) Burst behavior: we have frequent short bursts during triage hours (10–11am PST) — will the hosted probe reflect the elevated P95 we see in those windows? We want to understand how Redwood’s autoscaling and burst capacity compares to our hyperscaler setup where we already pay for reserved vCPU/GPU.

3) Compliance: can you confirm that any sample logs we share can stay within the Drive link you control and be deleted on request? We’ll need a DPA addendum before we share live PII-adjacent logs.

If those are fine, go ahead and schedule the benchmarking session. We prefer the us-west1 region.

— Rajiv
CTO, Nimbus Health

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: infer cost matrix, hyperscaler deltas, and next tests

Rajiv — good questions. I dug into the model and attached a short benchmark plan. Highlights and numbers (high-level, all $ per 1M input+output tokens):

Assumptions across scenarios
- Avg sequence length (input+output): 250 tokens
- Model family: open-llm-v2-medium quantized where applicable
- Traffic profile: 70% short-turn chat (median 80 tokens), 30% long form (median 800 tokens)

Scenario A — Redwood Hosted (continuous batching + KV cache)
- 10% cache hit: $8.2 per 1M tokens, p95 220ms
- 30% cache hit: $6.1 per 1M tokens, p95 245ms
- 60% cache hit: $4.7 per 1M tokens, p95 280ms

Scenario B — Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, no multi-tenant uplift)
- 10% cache hit: $6.7 per 1M tokens (committed pricing assumed), p95 180ms
- 30% cache hit: $5.0 per 1M tokens, p95 195ms
- 60% cache hit: $3.9 per 1M tokens, p95 210ms

Scenario C — Hyperscaler managed endpoints (your current setup)
- Observed uplift (typical) +35–65% at low volumes vs. dedicated (depends on instance sizing and autoscale thresholds)
- Ballpark: $9.0–$12.0 per 1M tokens for comparable latency SLA when you include reserved instance amortized cost and queuing inefficiencies

Notes on cache types
- Prefix/KV cache (conversational reuse) is the dominant win for your workload — it benefits more for repeated system prompts and clinician instruction sequences.
- Response-level dedup reduces output compute when identical outputs are returned (less common for patient-specific responses).

Burst behavior and test design
- The hosted probe will run an injected burst window to replicate your 10–11am triage spike; we’ll capture p50/p95/p99 and tail CPU/GPU utilization.
- For the dedicated run we’ll include a simulated cold pool startup to show worst-case p95 during burst.

Compliance and data handling
- We will only accept anonymized or hashed logs in the Drive folder. Redwood legal will provide a DPA addendum template.

Attachments: nimbus-multipass-benchmark-plan.md (contains step-by-step traffic scripts and targeted metrics).

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Rajiv: confirm anonymized dataset share + approve DPA path.
2) Irene: once dataset is confirmed, Ben will schedule a 2-hour bench window (we’ll share runbook and ephemeral Drive folder).
3) Marissa: if any commercial/legal guardrails are needed before running, please flag.

If helpful I can also run a quick sensitivity table for sequence length vs. per-1M token cost.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nimbus-multipass-benchmark-plan.md]
